Here are the first moves of a chess game:

1. e4 c6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. a3 Bxc3 5. bxc3 Nf6 6. f3 b6 7. d4 c5 8. d5 O-O 9. Ne2 Ba6 10. Nf4 exd5 11. cxd5 Bxf1 12. Rxf1 Re8 13. Kf2 d6 14. Kg1 Nfd7 15. c4 Ne5 16. Qc2 Qf6 17. g3 Nxc4 18. Rb1 Qd4+ 19. Kh1 Nd7 20. Rd1 Ne3 21. Bxe3 Qxe3 22. Rd3 Qxd3 23. Qxd3 Ne5 24. Qe2 a6 25. Rxb6 Reb8 26. Rxd6 Rb1+ 27. Kg2 Rab8 28. Kh3 R1b2 29. Qxa6 Nxf3 30. Qa5 Rxh2+ 31. Kg4 Ne5+ 32. Kf5 Re8 33. Rd8 g6+ 34. Kg5

It is black to move. Identify the shortest possible mating sequence in this position. Return the list of moves in standard chess notation and give just white and black's moves in order without the move numbers.

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: h6+ Kf6 Nd7#. h6+ is the forcing move: the g6-pawn covers f5 and the h2-rook cuts off h4/h5, so White’s king is compelled to go to f6. Then Nd7# brings the knight in with check, covering e5 and f8 while the e8-rook controls the e-file and the f7/g6/h6 pawns seal the remaining escape squares. The black king covers f7/g7, so White has no legal reply.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The king on g5 is completely shut in by the g-pawn and his own
knight on f4.

h2–h5 is open and 

    … Rh5+

is check on the 5th rank. 

* g6 is occupied by the black pawn,
* h5 is covered by …g6,
* h6 is covered by the rook on h5,
* f5 and h5 are covered by the rook on h5 and by …g6,
* f6 is covered by Nd7,
* h4 is covered by the rook on h5,
* g4 is covered by Ne5,
* f4 is occupied by the white Nf4.

The king cannot capture on h5 because h5 is protected by the g-pawn.
Hence

Rh5#
is mate in one, and therefore the shortest possible mating sequence.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The only checking move is the rook on h2. 
1… Rh5+ is the only check. The king cannot stay and cannot take on h5
because the pawn on g6 covers h5 and the knight on e5 covers g4.
2. Kf6 is the only king move that avoids the immediate capture
Nf4×h5.  After 2. Kf6 the e5–knight is now free from the a5–g5
self-pin and the rook can finish on the 5th rank.

2… Rf5#  Rook h5–f5 gives the vertical check on f6.  The check is
adjacent so it cannot be blocked.  K×f5 is illegal because the pawn
on g6 covers f5, K×e5 is illegal because Re8 covers e5, the only
interposition squares on the a5–g5 line are now irrelevant and
e7, f7, g7, e6, g6, e5, g5 are all covered by Re8, Ne5 and Kg8.
The line is therefore

Rh5+ Kf6 Rf5#

i.e. 1… Rh5+ 2. Kf6 3… Rf5# , a three-ply mate, the shortest mate
that can be obtained on the board.

So the first move must be a forcing check to f6. Both h6+ and Rh5+ force 35.Kf6.

* With Re8 on e8, e5, e6 and e7 are covered by Re8, f5 by g6-pawn, g5 by h6-pawn after h6+, f7/g7 by Kg8. The net is closed.
